title: Battery placement result
description: The placement server's answer for one scene (contract C2). Lengths are in feet; plan coordinates [x, z] and s follow scene.schema.json. The result settles placement only, never the whole installation: electrical checks (panel, meter) are outside it.

decision.description: pass: a fully observed spot passes every check under an approved policy. manual_review: a person must decide, because the best spot has an UNSURE check, the policy is not approved for automatic decisions, or an area that could hold a valid spot was not seen. reject: every spot within reach fails by a clear margin, and both ends of the walk are known.

summary.description: One sentence for the homeowner or reviewer.

auto_approve.description: Whether the rules allow automatic decisions: false when no policy is selected or the rules set auto_approve false (the public strict policy does, because some values are placeholders; the public demo policy decides anyway and says so in notice). When false, every would-be pass or reject becomes manual_review. Each check's rule.placeholder says which values decided it.

allow_reject.description: Whether the rules in use permit automatic rejections. When false, every would-be reject becomes manual_review with a policy_review_before_reject reason saying so.

rules_sha256.description: Hash of the merged rules the decision used.

notice.description: Whose rules these are, to show with the answer, for example that the public demo policy is not Base's. Null for rules that need no such label.

spot.description: The chosen battery position: the best passing spot, or for manual_review the best spot with no failing check. Null when no such spot exists, including every reject.

route.description: Cable route from the meter to the chosen spot. Null when `spot` is null.

checks.description: Every check at the chosen spot, or, when `spot` is null, at `nearest_considered`.

nearest_considered.description: When `spot` is null: the evaluated spot closest to passing (fewest failing checks, then fewest unsure, then shortest route), whose checks explain why it fails. Null otherwise.

missing_evidence.description: Views that would settle an UNSURE result. Only areas nobody observed appear here; an UNSURE caused by a measurement inside its error band needs a person, not more photos. Empty for pass and reject. Supplying exactly what a band request names settles it: a coverage.observed entry with the same band and span_ft, and out_ft at least the request's out_ft.

out_ft.description: For ground, facing, overhead and wall requests: how far the view must reach, out from the wall (ground, facing) or up from the ground (overhead, wall). Report it as the observed entry's out_ft; seeing further also settles it.

objects_not_used.description: Marked objects the server did not use: ones with no footprint past an unexplored end of the walk, where the wall may turn, so they have no known place. Tell the homeowner those marks weren't counted; walking further or giving them a footprint lets them count.

sweep.description: Outcome of every battery start position along the wall, merged into runs of equal outcome. Shows why each stretch fails; the site plan colours the wall with it.

segment.description: Straight baseline segment of `wall_id`; runs never cross a corner.

start_ft.description: Range of battery start positions (left edge, in s) in this run. Stretches too far along the wall for any cable route are one failing run, not evaluated start by start.

input_sha256.description: Hash of the scene JSON as uploaded.

s_ft.description: Where the wall chain ends, in s.

beyond_reach.description: True when this end is so far along the wall that no spot past it could pass the route-length check, so an unexplored end there does not block a reject.

id.description: Stable identifier, for example gas_clearance or route_length.

unsure_cause.description: Only for unsure. margin: measured inside the error band, a person must judge. unobserved: the deciding area was not seen, more photos fix it. unknown_attribute: a fact the camera did not establish (for example whether a window opens). rule_requires_review: the policy sends this situation to a person (for example a cable routed over a door).

measured_ft.description: The deciding measurement, for example the gap to the nearest gas meter. Null when nothing relevant was found or it was not observed.

review_threshold_ft.description: Present on checks with a review band (route_length): a value that doesn't clear this line (at_most: measured + error < review_threshold_ft) is at best unsure, even when it clears threshold_ft. Same convention as the scoring harness's review_threshold.

comparison.description: at_least: pass needs measured - error > threshold. at_most: pass needs measured + error < threshold.

subject.description: What the measurement is to, for example "objects[2] gas_meter".

placeholder.description: True for a demo value with no public source.

segment.description: Index of the straight baseline segment of `wall_id` the battery backs onto.

span_ft.description: Battery's stretch of wall in s, left edge first.

footprint.description: Plan corners [x, z]: back-left, back-right, front-right, front-left.

along.description: Unit vector along the wall toward +s.

outward.description: Unit vector from the wall out toward the battery's front.

meter_offset_ft.description: Footprint centre minus the meter's plan position, [dx, dz] in the scene frame's axes. scene.json carries no ground height, so the app sets the height by resting the box on its detected ground plane. Attach AR content to the meter's anchor with this offset, rotated by the anchor's orientation if the anchor is not axis-aligned with the scene frame.

length_ft.description: Length along the supported wall from the meter to the battery's near edge, including detours around wall objects.

height_ft.description: Height above ground the cable runs at, from the rules.

polyline.description: Plan points from the meter along the wall to the battery.

length_is_lower_bound.description: True when a detour object on the run had no recorded height, so the detour's length is unknown and length_ft is a floor, not a measurement. The path check names the object.
